observations.content: E-commerce platform is a monorepo with 4 services: storefront (Next.js), cart-service (Node.js), payment-service (Go), fulfillment-service (Python).
All services communicate via REST APIs; no message queue currently in use.
Current architecture handles ~500 orders/hour at peak.
Storefront is a Next.js 14 app with App Router, deployed on Vercel.
Storefront uses Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui component library.
Storefront has no server-side caching; every page load hits cart-service and product DB.
Storefront Lighthouse score: Performance 62, Accessibility 78, Best Practices 85, SEO 71.
cart-service is a Node.js Express app running on ECS Fargate.
cart-service stores cart state in DynamoDB with a 24-hour TTL.
cart-service has no authentication middleware — cart IDs are UUIDs passed as cookies.
payment-service is a Go service running on ECS, integrates with Stripe API.
payment-service processes refunds synchronously; average refund processing time is 8 seconds.
payment-service PCI compliance was last audited 2025-09-15; due for re-audit.
fulfillment-service is a Python FastAPI app running on ECS.
fulfillment-service integrates with ShipStation for label generation and tracking.
fulfillment-service has a 30-second timeout on ShipStation API calls; occasional timeouts during peak.
Product catalog is in PostgreSQL on RDS, db.r6g.xlarge, ~50,000 SKUs.
Product search uses pg_trgm extension for fuzzy matching; no dedicated search engine.
Product images are stored in S3 with CloudFront CDN; average image size 2.1MB (unoptimized).
Application monitoring uses Datadog APM on all services except fulfillment-service.
No distributed tracing across services — debugging multi-service issues requires manual log correlation.
Alert fatigue: 47 active alert rules, team reports ~60% are noise.
Business goal: support 5,000 orders/hour by Q3 2026 (10x current capacity).
Current bottleneck analysis: payment-service is CPU-bound during peak, cart-service DynamoDB reads throttle at ~800 orders/hour.
8 engineers total: 2 Go specialists (payment), 2 full-stack (storefront + cart), 2 Python (fulfillment), 2 platform/infra. No dedicated SRE.
Team uses 2-week sprints. Current velocity ~40 story points per sprint.
All services run on ECS Fargate except storefront (Vercel). RDS for PostgreSQL, DynamoDB for cart state.
No auto-scaling configured on ECS services; manual scaling during anticipated traffic spikes.
CI/CD via GitHub Actions. Average pipeline time: 18 minutes.
